summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science core: asymptotic analysis and recurrences, algorithms and data structures (divide and conquer, FFT-style ideas at the level of an algorithms course), discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, binary representation, induction, basic combinatorics), and linear algebra (vectors, matrices, bases, invertible maps, subspaces over the reals and complex numbers). They know basic Turing machines with tapes, but not multitape time-complexity subtleties, the Schönhage–Strassen or Harvey–van der Hoeven methods, number-theoretic transforms in depth, or any research-level algebra or numerical analysis.

known.name: Binary representation and bit operations
known.gloss: Integers are written as strings of bits, and bitwise operations such as XOR combine them coordinatewise modulo 2.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where numbers are identified when they differ by a multiple of a modulus.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: Two integers are coprime when their only common positive divisor is 1, and every integer factors into primes.

known.name: Matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: Linear maps between vector spaces represented by matrices, with composition, inverses and changes of basis.

known.name: Vector spaces over finite fields
known.gloss: Vector spaces whose scalars are the integers modulo 2, with subspaces, dimension and rank as in ordinary linear algebra.

known.name: Norms and triangle inequality
known.gloss: A norm measures size of a vector, satisfies the triangle inequality, and bounds the effect of a linear map on size.

known.name: Floor, ceiling, rounding and logarithms
known.gloss: Basic functions for rounding real numbers to integers and for base-2 logarithms used in bit-length and complexity bounds.

known.name: Recurrences and divide and conquer
known.gloss: Running time of a recursive algorithm is expressed by a recurrence and solved by summing costs over recursion levels.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and carries
known.gloss: The quadratic-time digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm with carries.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform
known.gloss: The divide-and-conquer algorithm computing a length-2^k DFT in O(N log N) arithmetic operations.

known.name: Euler's formula and exponentials of complex numbers
known.gloss: The complex exponential e^{iθ}=cos θ+i sin θ, giving unit-modulus phases and the roots of unity.

known.name: Gaussian function and Gaussian sums
known.gloss: The function exp(-x^2) with rapid decay, used as a smooth weight in interpolation and error estimates.

known.name: Geometric series and exponential decay bounds
known.gloss: Sums of terms decreasing by a constant ratio are bounded by a constant multiple of the first term.

known.name: Tuples, products of sets and mixed-radix indexing
known.gloss: Multi-dimensional arrays are indexed by tuples of coordinates and stored on a tape in a fixed order.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite set onto itself, applied to reorder the entries of an array.

known.name: Cyclic groups and direct products
known.gloss: The integers modulo q under addition form a cyclic group, and products of such groups index multi-dimensional cyclic arrays.

known.name: Real and complex number approximation
known.gloss: Real numbers are approximated by rationals with bounded error, and errors add under composed operations.

known.name: Big-O variants and constants
known.gloss: Asymptotic notations bounding growth from above, below or both up to constant factors.

known.name: Induction and proof by recursion
known.gloss: A proof technique establishing a statement for all sizes from a base case and a step.

known.name: Diagonal matrices
known.gloss: Matrices that scale each coordinate separately, equivalent to pointwise multiplication of a vector.
